newsitem.title: USA: Husband stabbed in New York despite court order.
newsitem.headline: Husband stabbed in New York despite court order.

text.p: A suburban New York man was stabbed to death Thursday, allegedly by his wife against whom a court order of protection had been filed, police said.
Thomas Overstreet, 22, died at a local hospital after being stabbed by his wife, Iliana Overstreet, 21, Nassau County, N.Y., police said.
The couple lived in a two-bedroom apartment with their 4-year-old daughter, who was not home at the time of the incident.

The stabbing occurred at 1:30 a.m. at the couple's basement apartment, police said. Overstreet staggered to a neighbour's house, where he knocked on the window and said, "Would you call the police? I've been stabbed in the back by my wife," police said.

Police had responded to a report of domestic violence at the apartment two hours before the stabbing. When they arrived, both the husband and wife said there was no court order of protection in place.
However, police said Overstreet may have not realised a Family Court order was in effect because a Criminal Court order of protection had been dismissed in November.
The protection orders stemmed from an earlier incident in which Overstreet was stabbed by his wife last April, police said. She was charged with assault in that case.
Had the police known of the order of protection, they would have arrested his wife, they said.
Following the stabbing, Iliana Overstreet jumped over a fence in the neighbourhood, leaped into a nearby canal and was found wandering wet on the street, police said.
She was treated for exposure and arrested on a charge of second-degree murder.
The couple had been high school sweethearts and married in 1992. Overstreet was the manager of a local delicatessen.
Iliana Overstreet was arrested twice before for violating the court order, and police said they have responded to calls of domestic violence at their home several times.
